subject: IRP packet request + walkthrough for SIG/CAIQ review
messages:
From: Sandra Lopez <sandra@veritab.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: BrightAudit SOC Team <soc2@brightaudit.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: IR artifacts + log slices for SIG/CAIQ mapping

Hannah —

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our SIG/CAIQ review for Veritab's integration, BrightAudit has asked for a short package with: the current Incident Response Plan summary, a mapping of SIG/CAIQ controls to your IR artifacts, and a 72-hour log slice around the recent elevated-auth event (UTC 2026-12-14 02:30 — 2026-12-16 02:30). They also want a short walkthrough (30 min) so they can validate the mappings.

Can you confirm what you can share (redacted where needed), how soon, and whether a walkthrough on Tue or Wed this week works?

- Sandra Lopez
Security Program Manager, Veritab
Attachment: verification_requirements_veritab.pdf (pdf)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sandra Lopez <sandra@veritab.com>
Cc: BrightAudit SOC Team <soc2@brightaudit.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: IR artifacts + log slices for SIG/CAIQ mapping

Sandra — thanks for the clear ask. We can provide: a one-page IRP summary, our SIG/CAIQ mapping CSV, and a sanitized log extract covering the 72-hour window. A few quick clarifications before we prepare the package: 

- Confirm whether BrightAudit needs raw logs (NDJSON) or CSV excerpts with indices/pseudonyms. We can deliver both but raw NDJSON will need an additional NDA clause for customer data.
- Any specific fields required (IP, user_id, session_id, request_path)? We typically include timestamp, event_type, user_id (pseudonymized), source_ip (CIDR truncated), and request_path.
- For the walkthrough: Tue 2026-12-15 10:00–10:30 PT or Wed 2026-12-16 09:00–09:30 PT work for us.

I'll loop in Marissa for the artifact pack and Karthik for retention/forensics details.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0191

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sandra Lopez <sandra@veritab.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightAudit SOC Team <soc2@brightaudit.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Request: IR artifacts + log slices for SIG/CAIQ mapping

Hannah / Sandra —

Attaching the initial evidence bundle for review. Files below are sanitized and scoped to the requested window. Where we removed customer-identifying strings we replaced them with stable pseudonyms to preserve replayability for the audit.

Attachments (sent):
- redwood_irp_summary_v2.pdf — 2-page runbook summary and escalation matrix.
- sig_caiq_mapping_2026-12.csv — mapping rows for SIG/CAIQ control ids to Redwood artifacts and owners.
- log_extract_20261214-20261216.ndjson — 72-hour event slice, IPs CIDR-truncated, user_ids pseudonymized.

Notes: 
- The NDJSON extract is compressed; if BrightAudit prefers a CSV excerpt we can produce a 20k-line sample with indices.
- We redacted request payloads for PII. For deeper forensic review we can arrange a secure, auditor-only transfer under an addendum.

Attachment stubs: redwood_irp_summary_v2.pdf (pdf), sig_caiq_mapping_2026-12.csv (csv), log_extract_20261214-20261216.ndjson (ndjson.gz)

-- 
Marissa Cole
Security Ops Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: Sandra Lopez <sandra@veritab.com>, BrightAudit SOC Team <soc2@brightaudit.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: IR artifacts + log slices for SIG/CAIQ mapping

Quick technical add: 

- Retention/coverage: our logging pipeline retains detailed application traces for 30 days and anonymized indices for 90 days. The 72-hour slice includes token-level events for inference requests (we remove request text payloads by default).
- Hashes: where required by auditors we can provide SHA256 hashes of omitted payloads to prove provenance without revealing content.
- Secure transfer: Recommend S3 presigned URL with auditor ACL (expires 72 hours) or a direct share via our locked Drive folder. Indicate preference and we will stage.

If auditors will need raw request bodies we need an NDA amendment (we rarely share raw request bodies due to customer data).

-Karthik
Lead, Platform Forensics

From: Sandra Lopez <sandra@veritab.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Thanks — this looks good. BrightAudit prefers NDJSON via a presigned S3 link (auditor-only) and hashed placeholders for omitted payloads; an NDA amendment is fine for raw request bodies but probably not necessary for this pass.

We can take Tue 2026-12-15 10:00 PT for the walkthrough. Please share the calendar invite with a brief agenda (10m mapping review, 15m log walkthrough, 5m Q&A).

Sandra

- redwood_irp_summary_v2.pdf (attached) — IR roles, escalation matrix, SLAs for incident notify.
- sig_caiq_mapping_2026-12.csv (attached) — controls → artifacts mapping with owners and evidence file pointers.

Thanks everyone —
Hannah Schmitt

Redwood Inference
